newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuban parliamentary president heads for U.S. talks.
newsitem.headline: Cuban parliamentary president heads for U.S. talks.

text.p: Cuban parliamentary president Ricardo Alarcon left on Sunday for New York, where he will head Cuba's side at talks with the United States on migration issues, Cuban state media said.

The talks, to be held this Wednesday and Thursday, are the latest in periodic discussions the United States and Cuba hold to review progress implementing their migration accords of May 1995 and September 1994. The last such round of talks was held in December in Havana.

Under the May 1995 agreement, Washington undertook to repatriate Cuban boat people intercepted trying to reach the United States, while at the same time boosting the number of visas it grants Cubans to 20,000 a year.

The aim, which has been largely achieved, was to halt a flow of Cuban boat people over the Florida Straits that reached crisis point in August 1994 when more than 30,000 Cubans left the communist-ruled island on flimsy rafts.

The migration talks are one of the very few areas in which Washington and Havana cooperate. The two countries, which have no diplomatic relations, have been political enemies since the 1959 revolution that brought Cuban President Fidel Castro to power.
